title: Bounded t-structures and canonical truncations on directed pair categories
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each $i\in I$ let $\mathcal C_i$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with a bounded t-structure [def-weil-t-structure]. For $i\le j$ supply exact t-exact functors $T_{j/i}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, where t-exact means preserving both halves in every degree. Take $T_{i/i}=1$, and supply exact natural associators $a_{k,j,i}:T_{k/j}T_{j/i}\cong T_{k/i}$ satisfying the identity and pentagon equations, compatible with the specified shift comparisons.

Form the pair category $P$ with objects $(i,K)$ and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_P((i,K),(j,L))=\varinjlim_{k\ge i,j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_k}(T_{k/i}K,T_{k/j}L).$$
The transition on arrows is $u\mapsto a_{r,k,j}T_{r/k}(u)a_{r,k,i}^{-1}$, and composition is calculated at a common stage. The colimit is the directed colimit of abelian groups [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. Assume $P$ is triangulated with shift $(i,K)[1]=(i,K[1])$, and distinguished triangles exactly those isomorphic to the image of a distinguished triangle at one stage, whose inclusions are exact.

Then the isomorphism closures of pairs $(i,K)$ with $K\in\mathcal C_i^{\le0}$ and with $K\in\mathcal C_i^{\ge0}$ form a bounded t-structure on $P$. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, its canonical truncations are represented by $(i,K)\mapsto(i,\tau_i^{\le m}K)$ and $(i,K)\mapsto(i,\tau_i^{\ge m}K)$. On an arrow represented by $u$ at $k$, their value is the class of $c_{k/j}^{-1}\tau_k(u)c_{k/i}$, where $c_{k/i}:T_{k/i}\tau_i\cong\tau_kT_{k/i}$ is the unique comparison preserving the canonical truncation map. These formulas are independent of representatives and stage. Canonical truncation maps and distinguished truncation triangles are represented by their stage versions. The comparisons $c$ respect identities and associators.

proof.text: Apply the proved StageSystem.tStructure to the stage t-structures, deriving its bound-preservation hypotheses from the given IsTExact instances. Its halves are the eventual stage bounds. If a pair has an eventual bound at stage j, isoToStage identifies it with the inclusion of its transported stage object. Conversely an isomorphism to an included bounded object gives the bound using t-exactness of the inclusion and isomorphism closure. Thus the eventual halves are exactly the stated isomorphism closures in every degree.

proof.text: The orthogonality and shift axioms are the ones proved in StageSystem.tStructure: any morphism is represented after a common stage at which both bounds hold, and stage orthogonality kills its representative. T-exactness propagates bounds and shift comparisons transport the shift axioms. No transition needs to reflect a bound or a morphism.

proof.text: The stage truncation triangle, mapped by the exact inclusion, is the existence axiom already supplied by StageSystem.tStructure. Define local IsTExact instances for the inclusions directly from the eventual-half predicates. For a pair (i,K), obtain the two bounds from the hypothesis (t i).bounded = top and transport each through its inclusion. This proves that the pair t-structure is bounded.

source.place: Definition 1.3.1(iii), p. 29, and boundedness by the objectwise bounds of the stages

proof.text: Use the existing eTruncLTIso and eTruncGEIso as cLE and cGE. The characterization and uniqueness clauses are lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison. For the identity transition, substitute its given equality with the identity functor and cancel the truncation counit or unit. For associator coherence postcompose the upper equation by the target counit, or precompose the lower equation by the twice-mapped source unit. Naturality of the associator and canonical maps proves the equalities, and truncation extensionality cancels these canonical maps. The lower cancellation is transported along the canonical truncation comparison.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i)-(ii), pp. 29-30; canonical t-exact comparisons and coherence as stated in the cited generic lemma

proof.text: Package each stage truncation with cLE or cGE as a StageSystem.Morphism S S; the associator coherence just proved is precisely its coherence field. Its existing functor on pair categories defines QLE and QGE, with literal object values and quotient-defined arrow maps. Componentwise comparisons for the t-exact inclusions give isomorphisms from these represented objects to the canonical pair truncations.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), pp. 29-30: comparisons for the now bounded t-exact inclusions; elementary conjugation of a functor

proof.text: The representative map formulas are definitional equalities for StageSystem.Morphism.functor and mapAt. Its quotient construction and tr_mapAt theorem already prove independence of representative and stage, and its functor laws are proved by common-stage composition. Thus no separate choice of an arrow representative is made.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), pp. 29-30: the cited comparison naturality and composition equations, followed by substitution and cancellation

proof.text: The characterization equations for cLE and cGE make the stage counits and units compatible StageSystem.Morphism.Hom families. Descend them using descNatTrans and identify the identity descended functor with the identity using functorIdIso. Their components are exactly the included stage maps. The inclusion comparison characterizations identify them with the canonical pair counit and unit. Extensionality for maps to truncLT and from truncGE proves that the componentwise inclusion comparisons are natural, giving bLE and bGE and the required canonical-map clauses.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), pp. 29-30: characterizing counit and unit equations of the existing comparison lemma

proof.text: Apply triangle_iso_exists to the canonical pair truncation triangle and the included stage truncation triangle, fixing the middle object by the identity. Both triangles are distinguished, with first object bounded above by m and third bounded below by m+1; the inclusion bounds follow from its local IsTExact instance. The first commutative square, the upper comparison characterization and counit cancellation identify the first component with bLE inverse. The second square and unit cancellation similarly identify the third component with bGE at m+1 inverse. Since this is an isomorphism of full triangles, its third square also identifies the connecting arrow.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(ii), pp. 29-30: characterization of the distinguished truncation triangle, including its unique degree-one arrow

It is still unsplit in live and in side-live, and neither it nor its citations are in the drop list. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live. There are no new nodes. The nine steps are 397-851 characters each (5979 in total). Every citation is a definition or the in-unit lemma lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison, so no tool_uses are needed. Sources read: the master and main-20261015 descent sentence (identical in both) and BBD 1.3.1/1.3.3 (PDF pp. 30-31). I compared the old parent steps 5-6 from the Q90 packet: every argument is carried here. The finite-field-only lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent is correctly replaced by conjugation with the comparison d_i for J_i, which works for an arbitrary directed poset. Step checks: (1) I recomputed e_{r/i}=J_r(a)e_{r/k}e_{k/i} at stage r, using the identity axiom a_{r,k,k}=1, and f=e^{-1}J_k(u)e. (2)-(4) Shift closure, orthogonality via Hom(A,B[-1]) with representatives at a common stage, the stage triangle under exact J_i, and objectwise boundedness all hold. (5) The coherence equation follows exactly from the natural-transformation clause with η=a_{r,k,i} and the composite clause. (6) All lemma hypotheses hold for J_i once step 4 gives a bounded t-structure on P. (7) I recomputed d_j^{-1}Q(f)d_i = e^{-1}J_k(c^{-1}τ_k(u)c)e and checked the types, which also gives independence of representative and stage. (8) These are the lemma's characterising equations. (9) The truncation triangle is unique up to an isomorphism fixing K (BBD 1.3.3(ii)); orthogonality forces its end components to be d^∓, so the connecting arrow is identified too. Small cases: one stage, a constant diagram, the zero category or a zero transition (which is why isomorphism closures are needed), and unbounded amplitudes across objects. Duplicates: lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations is only a specialisation to separated schemes, lem-a1-texact-coefficient-stage-descent assumes this t-structure, and the Lean StageSystem.tStructure states no boundedness or truncation formula, so it cannot be attached. The report correctly notes that the blueprint's claim 'truncations are exact triangulated' is false; it is not used. No SGA source and no fixes.
